notes: Round-2 blocking finding withdrawn. In `כִּי אַתָּה <j:conditional …/>הוּא<j:endConditional …/> אֱלֹהֵינוּ`, when hu=false, two whitespace characters touch in the character stream. In TEI mixed content with no xml:space="preserve" (none appears anywhere in the 22 files), a run of whitespace means a single word boundary, not a count of printed spaces. HTML white-space:normal and normal TeX typesetting both collapse it to one interword space. So it is not a printed double space and not a word-boundary defect. My round-2 claim that it was 'the same defect' as the round-1 אֵל נָא item was wrong as a rendering claim.

The current placement is the only one that is correct in all three states without putting a space inside the scope. hu=true gives 'אַתָּה הוּא אֱלֹהֵינוּ'. hu=false gives 'אַתָּה אֱלֹהֵינוּ' after collapse. Undefined/marked gives 'אַתָּה (הוּא) אֱלֹהֵינוּ'. My round-2 fix (a space inside the scope) would make the marked rendering at p.59 '(הוּא )' or '( הוּא)', which is a real extra space inside the brackets. Dropping both outer spaces would join words when hu=true.

This is different from real punctuation spacing. A space before a comma or colon stays visible after whitespace collapse, so the en `</tei:seg>…<tei:milestone unit="chapter"/>, O God.` fix (line 1143, no space before the comma) was a real correction and is correctly in place. In the he home, `<tei:milestone unit="chapter"/> אֵל נָא:` (line 576) has a single space before a word, which is correct.

Requirement for downstream code (no change needed in the XML): any plain-text export, search index, payload comparison or check that reads this text must normalize whitespace the same way your source-equality check does. An xml:space=preserve or white-space:pre consumer would show the double space, but that would be a consumer bug, not an encoding defect.
